name: Private object storage on Azure for synthetic documents
requirements: Private Azure Blob Storage for synthetic documents; existing service identity uploads/reads/deletes; no anonymous access; versioning; provider-managed encryption; candidate region australiaeast; no compute/AI/private endpoint; do not deploy.

data.label: Existing service identity
data.description: Existing service identity outside the provisioning scope. Its principal ID is supplied separately as a required input. It is not created or changed here, and it has not been verified.

data.label: Private document storage
data.description: Azure Storage account with a private container for synthetic documents, deployed into an existing resource group supplied as input. Anonymous/public blob access is disabled, blob versioning is enabled and encryption at rest uses Microsoft-managed keys. There is no compute and no private endpoint. Regional support for australiaeast is assumed, not verified.

brief.application: Design private object storage on Azure for synthetic documents. An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access and enable versioning. Use provider-managed encryption. Use australiaeast as a candidate region. No compute, AI or private network endpoint is needed for this first test. Existing account, resource group/project/COS instance and principal identifiers will be supplied separately. Draw a complete supported storage architecture with the explicit caller and access relationship. Do not deploy.

decisions.subject: design.private-azure-blob-storage-with-existing-service-identity
decisions.title: Private Azure Blob Storage with existing service identity
decisions.context: Scope: one Azure Blob Storage account and container for synthetic documents, using the private-object-storage contract. Public/anonymous blob access is blocked, blob versioning is enabled and encryption uses Microsoft-managed keys. The existing service identity (outside provisioning scope) gets scoped object upload, read and delete access through storage-object-admin. Assumptions: australiaeast is a candidate region, not a verified one. The existing resource group and principal identifiers will be supplied later as required inputs. No compute, AI or private endpoint is included. This is a design only and does not deploy anything.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Only the existing service identity can upload, read and delete objects in the container. All anonymous access is denied.
needs.rationale: Anonymous or too-broad access could expose documents. A tightly scoped role limits the damage if credentials leak.
needs.basis: User: "An existing service identity must upload, read and delete objects. Block anonymous access"

needs.statement: Blob versioning is enabled so objects can be recovered after an overwrite or delete. Data is encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys.
needs.rationale: Versioning protects against accidental deletes, which matters because the caller has delete rights. Retention of old versions affects storage cost.

needs.statement: Proposed: data residency country to be confirmed. australiaeast is only a candidate region.
needs.rationale: The country decides which regions are allowed and whether redundancy may copy data across borders.
needs.basis: User: "Use australiaeast as a candidate region"
